fighterA.name: Character A

dossier.style: Brutal, primal aggression. Atrocitus charges at opponents to physically tear them apart with bare hands, supported by searing rage plasma that burns through matter and space itself.
dossier.advantage: Red ring instead of a heart and inhuman strength. The ring keeps him alive even after fatal wounds, and his physical power allows him to crush energy barriers and deity armor with his bare hands.
dossier.mentality: Furious fanatic driven by revenge. Knows no mercy or hesitation – presses on with a fury that grows more powerful the more hatred and anger the enemy shows him.
dossier.quote: I am Atrocitus, lord and master of the Red Lantern Corps. I am the one who will destroy the Guardians and all they stand for. I am wrath, I am hate, I am righteous vengeance!

victories: Saint Walker, Indigo-1, and Star Sapphire

powers: Red Lantern plasma output, constructs, blood magic and rituals, flight, and Butcher-linked rage dynamics.
tools: Emotional-spectrum manipulation and high-pressure ranged offense.
weaknesses: Ring or construct-output dependence and front-loaded control windows.
Prolonged direct brawls can reduce his tactical edge.

crucialFeats: Bound the Butcher inside his power battery.
Burned through the fabric of space.
Overpowered Saint Walker, Indigo-1, and Star Sapphire.

dossier.style: Unstoppable close-quarters destruction. Relies on pure physical strength and constant forward momentum, crushing everything under his strikes.
dossier.advantage: Unlimited strength growth and regeneration. The more injured and angry he becomes, the stronger he gets, making him practically unbeatable in a fight of attrition.
dossier.mentality: Stubborn and wild destroyer. Does not calculate or retreat – presses on until every resistance is leveled with the ground.

powers: Gamma-based strength growth, regeneration, thunderclap/shockwave output, and extreme stamina.
weaknesses: Limited precision utility at long range versus dedicated control users.
Strategy set is narrower when denied sustained contact.

tactical-board.headline: TACTICAL BOARD // ATROCITUS VS HULK
tactical-board.subtitle: Butcher versus Worldbreaker
tactical-board.lane: Atrocitus wins by keeping the fight structured. Hulk wins by turning structure into a repeat contact loop.

battle-dynamics.headline: BATTLE DYNAMICS
battle-dynamics.subtitle: How the fight changes minute by minute.
battle-dynamics.left_curve_body: Stronger early, then weaker every time contact becomes repeatable.
battle-dynamics.right_curve_body: Starts lower, then rises fast once regeneration and re-entry stop caring about partial damage.

x-factor.headline: X-FACTOR
x-factor.subtitle: The variable that affects the verdict more than ordinary stats.
x-factor.left_body: If Atrocitus keeps Hulk at range and manages the fight from the outside, his plasma, rituals, and flight can stay ahead of the escalation curve.
x-factor.right_body: If Hulk forces repeat contact, rage control stops being a leash and starts becoming fuel for a stronger future exchange.
x-factor.implication: The winner is decided by whether rage remains externally managed or becomes self-sustaining gamma escalation.

interpretation.headline: INTERPRETATION
interpretation.subtitle: Who wins the fight on paper?
interpretation.question: Who wins the fight on paper?
interpretation.answer: Atrocitus wins the paper comparison, but Hulk still wins more real fights.
interpretation.body: Atrocitus owns the cleaner early toolkit, better speed, and stronger control options. Hulk owns the cleaner finish route once contact becomes repeatable. This is a matchup where the paper edge belongs to the more versatile side, but the practical edge belongs to the side whose loop gets stronger every time the control plan slips.

fight-simulation.headline: FIGHT SIMULATION
fight-simulation.subtitle: The course of the fight across three phases.
fight-simulation.phase_1_body: Atrocitus opens with flight, plasma, and blood-rage control to keep Hulk from building a simple rhythm.
fight-simulation.phase_2_body: Hulk absorbs the first control layer and keeps trying to collapse distance until the fight becomes physical anyway.
fight-simulation.phase_3_body: If Atrocitus keeps the fight external, he can stay ahead. If Hulk gets a second real contact sequence, regeneration and gamma escalation start erasing the value of every partial success.

stat-trap.headline: STAT TRAP
stat-trap.subtitle: Why better stats do not guarantee victory
stat-trap.question: Can Atrocitus keep Hulk's rage external, or does he end up feeding the loop himself?
stat-trap.body: Better averages do not matter if they do not create a finish route. Atrocitus has more ways to shape the opening, but Hulk gets more dangerous every time the fight resets into contact. This is not about who has more tools. It is about whose win condition stays intact after the first plan fails.

final-summary.headline: FINAL SUMMARY
final-summary.subtitle: Summary
final-summary.line_1: Atrocitus wins the paper comparison, 85.6 vs 83.9.
final-summary.line_2: Hulk wins more real fights because repeat contact and regeneration create the cleaner finish route.
final-summary.line_3: Atrocitus only flips the matchup if distance and control hold from start to finish.
